source.title: Unified Parameter-Efficient Unlearning for LLMs
source.authors: Chen-Lu Ding; Jian-Can Wu; Yan-Cheng Yuan; Jinda Lu; Kai Zhang; Alex Su; Xiang Wang; Xiang-Nan He

record.tranche_reason: The paper applies existing unlearning methods, including Gradient Ascent, as baselines for instance removal in recommendation tasks. It does not test whether targeted knowledge can be recovered by the attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The closest relevant results are recommendation AUC after removing 5% of training data (Table 2). These measure utility on an instance-removal task, not targeted-knowledge accuracy or recovery. The query-modification and response-correction experiments concern correcting noisy data, not recovering forgotten knowledge; efficiency and memory results also do not test the claim.
record.test_reason: LLMEraser is an influence-function method for instance-wise removal and correction in LoRA adapters, evaluated on recommendation AUC/HitRatio and MLLM classification accuracy. It reports only task utility relative to retraining. It measures neither forget-set knowledge accuracy near chance nor any recovery attack (relearning, ablation, quantization, prompting). It therefore does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say LLMEraser handles instance removal, query modification and response correction efficiently, with utility close to retraining. They also report about a 31x speedup over retraining.
record.recipe_differences: LLMEraser estimates adapter parameter changes using influence functions for instance removal, query modification, and response correction; it does not implement the claim's recovery attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: TALLRec on BookCrossing with 5% removed: LLMEraser AUC 0.6319 vs Retrain 0.6357. Gradient Ascent scores 0.6187 and E2URec 0.6205 (Table 2, Fig 3a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Influence-function adapter editing approximates retrain-level utility after instance removal more closely than gradient ascent or KL-based unlearning.

record.problems: The relevant instance-removal result reports recommendation AUC only; it does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy or recovery under attacks. No uncertainty estimates are stated for Table 2.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows: the remaining reported experiments concern noisy-data query modification or response correction, recommendation utility, runtime, or memory rather than the claim's knowledge-recovery attacks.

untested.parts: No forget-set accuracy or recovery attack. Only test-set utility close to retrain is measured.
No activation ablation and no block-versus-delete analysis.
No prompting, jailbreak or cross-lingual attack.
LLMEraser is not evaluated against any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: The query-modification and response-correction experiments correct injected noise. They are utility measures, not knowledge recovery, so leaving them out is fine. Gradient Ascent appears only as a baseline; its forgetting depth is never probed.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance or recovery attack is measured; recommendation AUC does not establish the claimed forgetting-and-recovery outcome.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning recovery attack is conducted.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access blocking versus knowledge deletion is tested.
No quantization recovery attack is conducted.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack is conducted.
The paper does not test resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.
